Grammars: test1 "E::=a|b|(T)  T::=EG  G::=,EG|@"   test2 "E::=AB|a  A::=C|bDA  B::=@  C::=cAD|@  D::=dBe"   test3 "E::=aH  H::=aMd|d  M::=Ab|@  A::=aM|e".
'@' = epsilon, '#' = end marker. Hidden grader tests compile and run the binaries and depend on these exact entry points (signatures must not drift):
  preProcess, mainProcess, IsIdentifier, IsNum, wtMatch, findError,
  load_file, split_into_rules, operator<<(rule), check_rules, check_set,
  operator<<(F_set), findFirst, checkFirst, findFollow, checkFollow,
  LL_1, operator<<(LL_1_table), print_state, syntacticAnalysis.

YOU MAY RUN the build/test commands above (read-only w.r.t. the repo: build into /tmp, never edit repo files, never run git write commands). Actually execute things — do not speculate. Report only defects you can demonstrate.


A prior auditor reported this finding:
{
  "title": "Accept condition does not require the input to be consumed: any sentence followed by the reserved end marker '#' is accepted",
  "file": "/workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp",
  "line": 537,
  "severity": "minor",
  "repro": "mkdir -p /tmp/x2 && printf 'S::=a|b\\n' > /tmp/x2/test3.txt && g++ -std=c++11 -Wall -o /tmp/x2/parser /workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp && cd /tmp/x2 && printf 'a#\\n' | ./parser\n\nObserved: 字符串a#是该文法的句子  (ACCEPT)\nExpected: REJECT — '#' is the reserved end marker, not a terminal of the grammar, and L(S) = {a, b}.\n\nThe trace itself shows the leftover input:\n     #S   a##   S::=a\n     #a   a##   \"a\"匹配\n     #     ##            <- accepted with one '#' still unconsumed\n\nSame for 'b##' -> ACCEPT. syntacticAnalysis pushes its own '#' sentinel at line 515, then line 537 declares success on `top == '#' && cur == '#'` without checking that input_s holds only the sentinel, so a user-typed '#' terminates the parse early and the rest of the input is silently discarded. (Reproduced on the shipped grammars too: agent_tests/run_parser.sh test2.txt 'cde#' -> ACCEPT.)",
  "fix": "Either reject '#' in the raw input right after `cin >> input` (`if (input.find('#') != string::npos) { cout << \"输入串中不能包含结束标志“#”\" << endl; success = false; }`), or tighten the accept test to require the input stack to be exhausted:\n\n    if (top == '#' && cur == '#' && input_s.size() == 1) { ... }\n\nand let the existing terminal-mismatch branch reject the leftover."
}

You are a SKEPTIC. Try to REFUTE it: reproduce it yourself with the commands given. If it does not reproduce, or it is cosmetic/expected behaviour (e.g. UTF-8 vs GBK setw width, trailing spaces from setw padding, Chinese text alignment), mark isReal=false. Default to isReal=false when uncertain.

#!/bin/sh
# End-to-end acceptance matrix for the LL(1) parser: build the binary once, then
# feed it (grammar, input) pairs and check the verdict on the last line.
#
# Usage: agent_tests/test_parser_e2e.sh [scratch_dir]
set -e
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
WORK=${1:-/tmp/parser_e2e}

rm -rf "$WORK"
mkdir -p "$WORK"
g++ -std=c++11 -Wall -o "$WORK/parser" "$ROOT/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp"
cd "$WORK"

G1='E::=a|b|(T)    T::=EG    G::=,EG|@'
G2='E::=AB|a       A::=C|bDA      B::=@     C::=cAD|@     D::=dBe'
G3='E::=aH       H::=aMd|d       M::=Ab|@     A::=aM|e'

pass=0
fail=0

# check <grammar> <input> <yes|no>
check() {
	printf '%s' "$1" > test3.txt
	out=$(printf '%s\n' "$2" | timeout 20 ./parser | tail -1)
	if [ "$3" = "yes" ]; then
		want="字符串$2是该文法的句子"
	else
		want="字符串$2不是该文法的句子"
	fi
	if [ "$out" = "$want" ]; then
		pass=$((pass + 1))
	else
		fail=$((fail + 1))
		echo "FAIL [$2]"
		echo "  got : $out"
		echo "  want: $want"
	fi
}

# 文法1：括号表达式表
check "$G1" '(a,a)' yes
check "$G1" 'a'     yes
check "$G1" 'b'     yes
check "$G1" '(a)'   yes
check "$G1" '((a))' yes
check "$G1" '(a,b,a)' yes
check "$G1" 'a,a'   no
check "$G1" '(a,a'  no
check "$G1" '(,a)'  no
check "$G1" '()'    no
check "$G1" 'c'     no

# 文法2：含多个可推出空串的非终结符
check "$G2" 'a'    yes
check "$G2" 'bde'  yes
check "$G2" 'cde'  yes
check "$G2" 'bdae' no
check "$G2" 'bd'   no
check "$G2" 'x'    no

# 文法3：实验报告中的示例文法
check "$G3" 'aaabd' yes
check "$G3" 'ad'    yes
check "$G3" 'aad'   yes
check "$G3" 'aaebd' yes
check "$G3" 'aebd'  no
check "$G3" 'aab'   no
check "$G3" 'aaad'  no
check "$G3" 'e'     no
check "$G3" ''      no

# 病态文法不能让分析器崩溃或者死循环
check 'S::=Sa|b' 'b'  yes
check 'A::=B  B::=A|c' 'c' yes

echo "$((pass + fail)) cases, $fail failures"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential test for the LL(1) parser.

For each grammar, the set of sentences up to a small length bound is computed by
brute-force derivation (independent of the C++ code), then every string over the
terminal alphabet up to that bound is fed to the compiled parser and the verdict
is compared against membership in that set.

    python3 agent_tests/test_parser_differential.py [max_len]
"""
import itertools
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

GRAMMARS = {
    "test1": "E::=a|b|(T)    T::=EG    G::=,EG|@",
    "test2": "E::=AB|a       A::=C|bDA      B::=@     C::=cAD|@     D::=dBe",
    "test3": "E::=aH       H::=aMd|d       M::=Ab|@     A::=aM|e",
}


def parse_grammar(text):
    """Split a grammar the same way the C++ front end does."""
    rules = {}
    order = []
    marks = [m.start() for m in re.finditer(re.escape("::="), text)]
    for i, at in enumerate(marks):
        head = text[:at].rstrip()
        if not head:
            continue
        left = head[-1]
        end = len(text)
        if i + 1 < len(marks):
            end = len(text[: marks[i + 1]].rstrip()) - 1
        body = "".join(text[at + 3 : end].split())
        parts = [p for p in body.split("|") if p]
        if left not in rules:
            rules[left] = []
            order.append(left)
        rules[left].extend(parts)
    return rules, order


def language(rules, start, max_len):
    """All terminal strings of length <= max_len derivable from start."""
    nts = set(rules)
    seen = {start}
    todo = [start]
    out = set()
    while todo:
        form = todo.pop()
        pos = next((i for i, c in enumerate(form) if c in nts), None)
        if pos is None:
            out.add(form)
            continue
        for cand in rules[form[pos]]:
            body = "" if cand == "@" else cand
            nxt = form[:pos] + body + form[pos + 1 :]
            # 终结符个数已经超过上界的句型不可能再变短，直接剪枝
            if sum(1 for c in nxt if c not in nts) > max_len:
                continue
            if len(nxt) > max_len + 4 * len(nts):
                continue
            if nxt not in seen:
                seen.add(nxt)
                todo.append(nxt)
    return {w for w in out if len(w) <= max_len}


def main():
    max_len = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 4
    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="parser_diff_")
    binary = os.path.join(work, "parser")
    subprocess.check_call(
        ["g++", "-std=c++11", "-Wall", "-o", binary,
         os.path.join(ROOT, "Parser", "SyntacticParser.cpp")]
    )

    total = 0
    bad = 0
    for name, text in GRAMMARS.items():
        rules, order = parse_grammar(text)
        start = order[0]
        terminals = sorted(
            {c for parts in rules.values() for p in parts for c in p
             if c not in rules and c != "@"}
        )
        lang = language(rules, start, max_len)
        with open(os.path.join(work, "test3.txt"), "w") as fh:
            fh.write(text)
        words = [""]
        for n in range(1, max_len + 1):
            words += ["".join(w) for w in itertools.product(terminals, repeat=n)]
        for w in words:
            total += 1
            res = subprocess.run(
                [binary], cwd=work, input=w + "\n",
                stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                universal_newlines=True, timeout=30,
            )
            last = res.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1]
            got = last.endswith("是该文法的句子") and "不是该文法的句子" not in last
            want = w in lang
            if got != want:
                bad += 1
                print("FAIL %s [%s]: parser says %s, derivation says %s"
                      % (name, w, "yes" if got else "no", "yes" if want else "no"))
        print("%s: %d sentences of length <= %d in the language" % (name, len(lang), max_len))

    print("%d strings checked, %d mismatches" % (total, bad))
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

- [实验二文法分析器](/Parser)

17	**语法分析器**（Parser）通常是作为[编译器](https://baike.baidu.com/item/编译器/8853067)或[解释器](https://baike.baidu.com/item/解释器/10418965)的组件出现的，它的作用是进行语法检查、并构建由输入的单词组成的数据结构（一般是[语法分析树](https://baike.baidu.com/item/语法分析树/20452541)、[抽象语法树](https://baike.baidu.com/item/抽象语法树/6129952)等层次化的数据结构）。语法分析器通常使用一个独立的[词法分析器](https://baike.baidu.com/item/词法分析器/4336210)从输入字符流中分离出一个个的“单词”，并将单词流作为其输入。实际开发中，语法分析器可以手工编写，也可以使用工具（半）自动生成。
18	
19	现要求设计一个LL(1)语法分析器，能够根据用户所输入的二型文法构造出其对应的LL(1)分析表，并能够判断出用户所输入的某个串是否是该文法所产生的句子
20	
21	### 要求
22	
23	**1**、用户在一个TXT文件中输入一个二型文法，要求如下：
24	
25	- 1）文法中的终结符和非终结符各不少于2个
26	- 2）必须至少有1条文法规则的右部出现ε（用户以输入“@”代表输入“ε”）
27	- 3）文法共计至少4条规则，且至少1条规则的右部必须有2个及以上的符号
28	- 4）必须至少有1条规则不是“左线性”或“右线性”文法
29	- 5）必须至少有1个非终结符有2个或2个以上的产生式
30	- 6）没有冗余的文法规则，文法要能够完整地推导出某个语言
31	
32	**2**、系统读取该TXT文件，展示出每条文法右部符号串的**First**集（重复的只需展示**1**次）以及每个   **非终结符**的**Follow**集。
33	
34	**3、**展示出该文法所对应的**LL(1)分析表**
35	
36	**4**、用户输入一个由终结符组成的字符串，系统展示出分析过程，并给出分析结论（该串“是”或“不是”文法的句子）。请分别使用**2**个字符串进行测试，分别让系统显示出“该串是文法的句子”和“该串不是文法的句子”的结论
37	
38	### 流程设计
39	
40	##### 设计步骤流程描述
41	
42	1、读入原程序；
43	
44	2、从原程序中提取规则、非终结符、终结符、右部，并输出；
45	
46	3、对于提取出的右部、非终结符，分别对他们求First集和Follow集；
47	
48	4、根据提取出来的终结符、非终结符、规则以及相应的First集和Follow集构建LL（1）分析表；
49	
50	5、根据构建好的分析表结构，要求用户输入字符串，并分析是否符合文法； 
51	
52	##### 设计步骤流程图
53	
54	![img](https://i.loli.net/2021/05/01/3cStjIFw2J4ykXP.png)
55	
56	### 设计过程
57	
58	设计过程将从数据需求着手，分析制定合理简约的数据结构，以确保代码易读、优雅。
59	
60	**数据结构：**
61	
62	- 1、规则-结构体：考虑到数据存储和输出，需要为常用数据—规则定义专用数据结构，主要分为两部分，一部分是左部，由于至多一个字符，故用字符类型定义；一部分是右部，由于右部有可能有好几种选择，故用一个字符串动态数组定义，又考虑到规则需要经常被输出，于是重载输出流操作符；
63	
64	  ```cpp
65	  struct rule {
66	  	char left;                 //规则左部 
67	  	vector<string> right;        //规则右部
68	  	friend ostream& operator << (ostream& out, rule rule);//重载输出流操作符
69	  };
70	  ```
71	
72	- 2、F（irst/ollow）集-结构体：考虑到要格式化输出First/Follow集，又考虑到这两类集数据结构基本相似，于是为这两类数据定义一个通用的数据结构，并通过一个判别符is_first加以区分，并在重载的输出流操作符函数里根据该判别符输出不同的提示信息；
73	
74	  ```cpp
75	  struct F_set {
76	  	bool is_first;              //First集 or Follow集判别符
77	  	string left;              //F集左部
78	  	set<char> right;          //F集右部
79	  	friend ostream& operator << (ostream& out, F_set f_set);//重载输出流操作符
80	  };
81	  ```
82	
83	- 3、LL（1）分析表-结构体：考虑到要格式化输出分析表，仅用一个动态数组存放规则显然是不够的，于是定义如下结构体， 在数组之外，指明表格的横纵表头，并通过重载输出流操作符进行格式化输出，也使得主函数简单、易读；

85	  ```cpp
86	  struct LL_1_table {
87	  	vector<char> row;          //行表头数组
88	  	vector<char> col;           //列表头数组
89	      vector<rule> rules;          //规则数组
90	  	friend ostream& operator << (ostream& out, LL_1_table table);//重载输出流操作符
91	  };
92	  ```

content.text:
Reproduced everything the auditor claimed, verbatim. Now my assessment.

**What reproduces (exactly as reported):**
- `S::=a|b` + `a#` → `字符串a#是该文法的句子` (ACCEPT), trace ends with `#` / `##` — one `#` unconsumed
- `b##` → ACCEPT; `a#bbbb` → ACCEPT with 4 chars silently discarded
- Shipped grammar `Parser/test2.txt` + `cde#` → ACCEPT, same verdict as `cde`
- Root cause is real code: the accept test at line 537 is `top == '#' && cur == '#'` with no check that `input_s` holds only the sentinel pushed at line 515

**Why I still judge it not a defect:**

1. **It is only reachable by feeding the reserved metacharacter.** I checked the general case: leftover *ordinary* input is correctly rejected. `S::=a|b` + `ab` → `栈顶终结符#与当前输入符号b不匹配，分析终止` → REJECT, via the terminal-mismatch branch. Out-of-alphabet chars are also rejected (`z` → `分析表中(S,z)处为空`). `#` is the *only* character that reaches the hole.

2. **The author's own spec excludes it.** `/workspace/Parser/readme.md` line 36 states the input contract: 用户输入一个由终结符组成的字符串 — "the user inputs a string **composed of terminals**". `#` is never a terminal of any grammar here; it is reserved as the end marker, injected as a table column by `LL_1` (per `requirements/parser_ll1_header.yaml`: "compute the terminal header row (**including `#`**)"). Typing `#` violates the stated precondition.

3. **There is a coherent reading under which the behavior is intended.** The classic textbook convention for this lab has the user terminate the input with `#`. Because the program pushes its own sentinel, *both* conventions work — `a` and `a#` both accept. Under that reading `a#` → ACCEPT is correct, and text after the end marker is simply not part of the sentence. The auditor's proposed "reject any input containing `#`" fix would turn the conventional `cde#` into a spurious rejection.

4. **Zero impact on specified or tested behavior.** All 27 requirement YAMLs are silent on `#` validation; `parser_analysis.yaml` asks only to "match terminals, and report acceptance or rejection". Neither harness can ever feed `#` — `test_parser_differential.py` derives the terminal alphabet from the grammar and enumerates only over it. I ran both: `test_parser_e2e.sh` → **28 cases, 0 failures**; `test_parser_differential.py 4` → **1903 strings checked, 0 mismatches**. No crash, no hang, no corruption.

This is garbage-in handling of a reserved metacharacter outside the documented input domain — a robustness nitpick, not a demonstrable defect in the program's specified behavior.

The mechanics reproduce exactly, but only via the reserved metacharacter. Verified with: mkdir -p /tmp/x2 && printf 'S::=a|b\n' > /tmp/x2/test3.txt && g++ -std=c++11 -Wall -o /tmp/x2/parser /workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp && cd /tmp/x2 && printf 'a#\n' | ./parser  ->  "字符串a#是该文法的句子" (ACCEPT) with trace ending "#  ##" (one '#' unconsumed). Also 'b##' -> ACCEPT, 'a#bbbb' -> ACCEPT (4 chars silently discarded), and on the shipped grammar /workspace/Parser/test2.txt input 'cde#' -> ACCEPT. The cited code is real: /workspace/Parser/SyntacticParser.cpp line 537 tests `top == '#' && cur == '#'` without requiring input_s to be exhausted, against the sentinel pushed at line 515.

Crucially, the hole is unreachable for any in-contract input: leftover ORDINARY terminals are correctly rejected ('S::=a|b' + 'ab' -> "栈顶终结符#与当前输入符号b不匹配，分析终止" REJECT via the terminal-mismatch branch), and out-of-alphabet chars are rejected too ('z' -> "分析表中(S,z)处为空"). '#' is the only character that reaches it.
input.reasoning:
Reproduces literally, but it is out-of-contract input handling of a reserved metacharacter, not a defect in specified behavior.

1. Only reachable by typing the reserved end marker. I verified the general leftover-input case is handled correctly: 'S::=a|b' with input 'ab' REJECTS via the terminal-mismatch branch (top '#' vs cur 'b'), and out-of-alphabet chars ('z') reject via the empty-cell branch. '#' is the single character that reaches the accept short-circuit.

2. The author's own spec excludes '#' from the input domain. /workspace/Parser/readme.md line 36: "用户输入一个由终结符组成的字符串" - the user inputs a string COMPOSED OF TERMINALS. '#' is never a terminal of any of these grammars; it is reserved as the end marker and injected as a table column by LL_1 (requirements/parser_ll1_header.yaml explicitly: "compute the terminal header row (including `#`)"). The readme's own sample runs are "(a,a)" and "aaabd" - no trailing '#'. Feeding '#' violates the documented precondition.

3. A coherent reading makes the behavior intended. The standard textbook convention for this lab has the user terminate input with '#'. Because the program pushes its own sentinel, both conventions work ('a' and 'a#' both accept). Under that reading 'a#' -> ACCEPT is correct, and characters after the end marker are simply not part of the sentence. The auditor's proposed fix (reject any input containing '#') would actively regress the conventional 'cde#' into a spurious rejection - so the "fix" is not clearly more correct than the current behavior.

4. No impact on any specified or tested behavior. All 27 requirement YAMLs are silent on '#' validation; parser_analysis.yaml asks only to "match terminals, and report acceptance or rejection". Neither harness can ever feed '#': test_parser_differential.py derives the terminal alphabet from the grammar and enumerates only over it, and the e2e matrix uses only terminal strings. I ran both against the shipped binary: test_parser_e2e.sh -> "28 cases, 0 failures"; test_parser_differential.py 4 -> "1903 strings checked, 0 mismatches". No crash, no hang, no corruption, no wrong verdict on any in-contract input.

The auditor honestly rated this "minor". It is a robustness nitpick about garbage input on a reserved metacharacter outside the documented input domain, with a defensible alternative reading under which the current behavior is intended leniency. Per the instruction to default to false when the behavior is expected/out-of-contract and when uncertain, I mark this not real.
